attacks.claim: The embargo badge text is hard-coded #ffffff on background var(--surface), which is #ffffff in the default light theme. The label is white on white (~1:1), invisible, and fails WCAG 1.4.3. This defeats the badge's purpose.

The unpublish control is a non-focusable span with only a mouse onClick. It has no role, tabIndex, or key handler, so keyboard-only editors cannot reach it (WCAG 2.1.1). The icon is aria-hidden and there is no accessible name, so screen-reader users cannot identify the destructive action. There is also no :focus-visible style.
attacks.evidence: ; ABSENT: role, tabIndex, aria-label, onKeyDown, :focus-visible

attacks.claim: handleUnpublish awaits onUnpublish with no error handling or feedback. If the request fails after confirmation, the rejection is unhandled and the live story stays published while the editor may believe it was pulled. Nothing guards against re-entry or shows a pending state while the request is in flight.

Unpublish is gated only by client-side rendering. The diff does not show the server-side permission check, though it is likely in the existing onUnpublish API. This is worth confirming but is not evidenced as missing.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: server-side authorization for unpublish in the diff

attacks.claim: The embargo state is computed from the client clock at render time with no refresh. The badge can go stale or be wrong under clock skew.
attacks.evidence: const embargoed = draft.embargoUntil !== null && new Date(draft.embargoUntil) > new Date();

attacks.claim: The embargo time shows no timezone label. A trash icon for unpublish reads as delete. The PR description says 'one-click' although a confirm dialog is required, and says 'each queue row' although the control shows only for published drafts.
